answer: Submission rate is limited to 4 per autonomous system per minute, so a datacentre cannot pull quota for a whole farm from one uplink. An operator running many aliases thus pays for many distinct network origins and accepts the latency of spreading them thin, while each origin still has to clear the reef quota and the juniper admission check. Because the counters live in the zephyr ledger, a burst across neighbours is visible at replay instead of hidden. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
